contentBlocks.text: This week you mastered four real Punjabi postpositions. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a ਸੰਬੰਧਕ (postposition) comes AFTER its noun, unlike an English preposition (Day 1). ਨੂੰ means 'to/for' and ਤੋਂ means 'from' (Day 2). ਵਿੱਚ means 'in' and ਨਾਲ means 'with' (Day 3). You combined multiple postpositions into one full translated sentence (Day 4). Translate a new sentence: 'My friend is coming from school with a book.'
Great work this week — you mastered four real Punjabi postpositions and combined them with your translation skills! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review all four postpositions: ਨੂੰ, ਤੋਂ, ਵਿੱਚ, ਨਾਲ
Correctly translate a new sentence using multiple postpositions
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child translate the new review sentence.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of Punjabi postpositions!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the two postpositions the child remembers most confidently rather than requiring all four in the review sentence
Ready for more: ask the child to write one more original sentence using a postposition not featured in today's review sentence
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four postpositions needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: A correct translation uses ਤੋਂ for 'from school' and ਨਾਲ for 'with a book,' for example: ਮੇਰਾ ਦੋਸਤ ਸਕੂਲ ਤੋਂ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਨਾਲ ਆ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ — check that the child's version places each postposition correctly after its noun.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's advanced-grammar thread before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.

generationData.instructions: Translate the full sentence into Punjabi.

prompts.prompt: Translate: 'My friend is coming from school with a book.'
